summary.name: Hiring Your First SRE
summary.one_liner: A guide for hiring managers and interviewers on what a Site Reliability Engineer does and which topics and questions to use when interviewing one for a growing startup.
use_cases: Deciding whether to hire an SRE instead of more DevOps engineers
Writing interview questions for an SRE candidate
Explaining the SRE role to non-technical stakeholders
Planning monitoring, alerting, and on-call for a startup
summary.what_it_does: The article explains that an SRE is a systems developer focused on infrastructure problems and contrasts the role with DevOps, which it says is overused as a term. It organizes interview guidance into topics: reliability, monitoring, alerting, infrastructure, product engineering, debugging, and security. Each topic includes example questions to ask candidates. It also suggests that interviewers treat the interview as a collaborative conversation and check whether candidates debug with rigor. It gives general development and metrics/logging questions as well.
notable: Organized interview question list by topic (reliability, monitoring, alerting, debugging, security)
Written by an SRE who was often the first engineer hired at a company
Points to Google's SRE book and an interview with Ben Treynor for further reading
caveats: Written as opinion and experience rather than a formal hiring standard
Says more articles will follow, so the page covers only part of the topic
